    引入了通过 claude plugin test 运行的模组原位单元测试，并基于官方插件声明进行类型检查，提升了第三方插件开发的可测试性和类型安全性。

  3. #93951: 将 diff、sec-default 和 telemetry 的测试文件移至模组旁
    将模组测试文件 relocated 到 mods/<mod>/tests/ 目录下，与各模组放在一起，符合标准插件项目结构，方便贡献者针对单个模组开展工作。

  4. #93452: mods/diff：匹配内置 /diff 面板
    让 diff 模组的 UI 与内置 /diff 面板对齐（包括代码块渲染、控件、响应式行为），确保原生和基于插件的 diff 体验功能一致。

  5. #89404: validate-agent.sh：不要在首次警告时中止，停止对合法代理的误标记
    修复了插件开发技能的验证脚本：因 set -euo pipefail 的边缘情况，该脚本会对合法代理文件报错。这消除了插件开发者的一大阻碍。

  6. #79148: 为示例规则文件名添加强制的 hookify. 前缀
    修复了 hookify 示例规则因缺少必需的文件名前缀而静默失败的问题，纠正了文档偏差，提升了规则开箱即用的可用性。

  7. #63686: 将过期和自动关闭超时时间从 14 天延长至 90 天
    将 Issue 生命周期从 14 天延长至 90 天，减少过早标记为过期/关闭带来的干扰，让社区 Issue 有更多时间被分流和处理。

  8. #26175: 修复原生安装程序引导脚本故障
    修复了 curl | bash 安装流程的问题：该流程会静默失败，无法创建 ~/.local/bin/claude 二进制文件，还会删除现有的 npm 安装，导致用户没有可用的 CLI。

  9. #42205: fix(hookify): 标准化工具匹配器解析
    对 hookify 工具匹配器字符串做了裁剪和标准化处理，修复了分隔符前后有空格时匹配失败的问题，提升了规则匹配的健壮性。

  10. #61716: 新增上下文溢出导致虚假使用量限制的故障排查说明
    记录了一种常见的误导性错误：上下文溢出被误报为使用量限制，并添加了变通方法指导，解决了用户经常遇到的困惑点。

未提供讨论数据，本节省略。

6. 功能需求趋势

  1. 改进插件/模组开发工具：模组框架 PR 和插件验证修复的激增，契合了对更 robust、文档更完善的插件构建、测试和分发工具日益增长的需求。
  2. 细粒度的安全/AUP 过滤控制：安全从业者提交的大量 ClAudit 误报报告，反映出对白名单、领域专属过滤调优或自托管过滤策略自定义的需求。
  3. 更好的成本和使用量透明度：网关定价同步和上下文溢出使用量限制文档修复，体现了对更准确、可解释的成本追踪和使用量计量的需求。
  4. Windows 跨平台一致性：持续存在的 Windows 桌面端启动、进程和壳层集成 Bug，表明用户需求优先提升 Windows 平台质量和测试投入。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. Windows 平台不稳定：残留进程锁、作业对象泄漏和 Git Bash PATH 问题，导致 Windows 桌面端和壳层体验不可靠，变通方法需要重启或手动清理进程。
  2. 安全工作的安全过滤过于激进：防御性安全、取证和管理任务经常触发误报导致会话中断，干扰合法工作，给关注安全的用户带来阻碍。
  3. 插件开发体验粗糙：规则静默失败、验证脚本故障和文档不一致，为构建和调试自定义插件与钩子制造了障碍。
  4. 误导性错误信息：上下文溢出被误报为使用量限制、安装静默失败等问题，给终端用户带来不必要的困惑和调试时间。
  5. Issue 生命周期过短：之前 14 天的过期/自动关闭窗口过于激进，导致合法的社区 Issue 在被分流前就被关闭。

  1. 会话状态控制： 原生回退/撤销、按 PR 持久化会话是最受需求的工作流功能。
  2. 远程与编排体验： 无头守护进程模式、优化的 ChatGPT 应用远程控制、多实例工作器编排。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. Windows 平台不稳定： 绝大多数高优先级 Bug 都集中在 Windows 平台，涵盖沙箱失败、WSL 集成、认证、进程泄漏、应用服务器状态损坏等问题。
  2. 配额不透明与异常消耗： 用户反馈存在不明原因的快速用量消耗、Codex Chronicle 等进程后台静默消耗配额、重置规则不清晰等问题。

  4. API 密钥认证限制多： 浏览器控制、「代我批准」权限等功能在 API 密钥认证下不支持，导致功能碎片化。
  5. 缺少基础编辑原语： 没有原生回退/撤销功能，用户每次修改都得依赖 Git 提交，拖慢迭代速度。

3. 热门问题

  1. #22323 Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS reports GOAL success
    P1 级 bug，13 条评论，2 👍
    codebase_investigator 子代理即使达到最大轮次限制仍未完成分析，也会错误地返回 status: success 和 Termination Reason: GOAL。这会误导用户对任务完成状态的判断，是本周讨论最活跃的问题。

  2. #21409 Generalist agent hangs indefinitely
    P1 级 bug，8 条评论，8 👍（点赞数最高）
    简单任务（如创建文件夹）委派给通用代理时会永久挂起；禁用子代理后问题解决。由于基础功能故障，对社区影响较大，也是本周用户点赞数最高的问题。

  3. #19873 Zero-Dependency OS Sandboxing & Post-Execution Intent Routing
    P2 级增强需求，9 条评论，1 👍
    提出利用 Gemini 3 原生的 bash 适配性，通过零依赖操作系统沙箱使用 POSIX 工具链，在模型偏好的工作流与安全性之间取得平衡。这是未来代理执行架构的核心讨论方向。

  4. #25166 Shell command execution stuck on "Waiting input" after completion
    P1 级核心 bug，4 条评论，3 👍
    简单 shell 命令执行完成后仍显示“等待用户输入”而挂起。这是核心 shell 执行功能的关键可靠性问题。

  5. #22745 Assess AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping
    P2 级特性史诗，7 条评论，1 👍
    跟踪对 AST 感知工具的调研，用于实现精确的方法级读取、减少 token 冗余并加快代码库导航速度。这是代码库分析性能的重要潜在升级方向。

  6. #26525 Add deterministic redaction and reduce Auto Memory logging
    P2 级安全 bug，5 条评论
    Auto Memory 会在机密信息脱敏前将对话内容发送给模型，存在敏感数据在模型上下文和日志中泄露的风险。这是一个重要的安全与隐私缺口。

  7. #21968 Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents autonomously
    P2 级代理 bug，6 条评论
    用户反馈模型从不会自主调用自定义技能/子代理，即使是高度相关的任务（如 gradle/git 操作）也需要明确指令。这降低了自定义代理生态的实用性。

  8. #26522 Stop Auto Memory from retrying low-signal sessions indefinitely
    P2 级代理 bug，4 条评论
    被提取代理跳过的低信号会话仍标记为未处理，并被反复重新处理，浪费算力并降低记忆系统效率。

  9. #22267 Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (maxTurns, etc.)
    P2 级代理 bug，3 条评论
    浏览器子代理无视全局/项目 settings.json 中的配置（如 maxTurns），尽管 AgentRegistry 已正确合并设置。这打破了用户对专用代理配置的预期。

  10. #21335 /compress command not persistent across session resume
    P2 级代理 bug，2 条评论，2 👍
    /compress 生成的聊天摘要仅存储在内存中，不会写入磁盘，因此恢复会话时压缩状态会丢失。用户跨会话的 token 节省效果失效。

4. 重点 PR 进展

  1. #29286 Implement Google search tool in RobustAutonomousAgent
    优先级 P1，规模 M，开放中
    为 RobustAutonomousAgent 添加原生 Google 搜索能力，支持实时网页查询，补充代码库和通用知识任务。

  2. #29163 Fix crash during authentication in git repositories
    优先级 P1，安全领域，规模 L，开放中
    修复在 macOS Seatbelt 或权限受限环境下的 Git 仓库中运行 Gemini CLI 时的启动崩溃问题，该问题由 useGitBranchName 钩子无法访问 .git 目录导致。

  3. #29319 Guard JSON.parse on tool-call args in sendStream
    优先级 P2，非交互领域，规模 M，开放中
    通过为 JSON.parse 添加 try/catch 包装，修复格式错误的工具调用 JSON 导致的流终止问题；出现错误时会推送 _parseError 参数并继续流传输，而非直接崩溃。修复 #29308。

  4. #29320 Register express.json before A2A routes so req.body is parsed
    优先级 P2，代理领域，规模 S，开放中
    通过将 express.json() 中间件移至路由注册之前，修复 A2A 服务器路由的 JSON-RPC 解析失败问题，确保 A2A 端点的 req.body 能被正确填充。修复 #29315。

  5. #27863 Prioritize structured display titles in tool invocation
    优先级 P1，非交互领域，规模 S，开放中，寻求贡献
    更新 getDisplayTitle() 逻辑，优先使用 _toolDisplayName 而非原始工具名称，提升带有友好标签的自定义工具的 UI 清晰度。修复 #23018。

  6. #27754 Add missing return after 501 response in GET /tasks/metadata
    优先级 P1，核心领域，规模 XS，开放中，寻求贡献
    修复 A2A 服务器崩溃问题（ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT），该问题由 501 响应后缺少 return 语句，导致执行流程继续落入后续响应逻辑引发。修复 #21729。

  7. #29304 Avoid splitting surrogate pairs during truncation
    核心领域，规模 S，开放中
    修复 sanitizeForDisplay 函数，在文本截断时保留 UTF-16 代理对（如表情符号），防止截断位置落在多码元字形中间时导致字符静默丢失。

  8. #29208 Fall back to empty on malformed agents.json shape
    优先级 P2，代理领域，规模 S/M，开放中
    优雅处理损坏的 agents.json（如保存中断、同步冲突等导致的格式无效），改为回退到空状态，而非抛出 TypeError 崩溃或静默丢失确认信息。修复 #29207。

  9. #28963 Correct excludeTools examples that never match
    文档类，规模 S，开放中
    修复扩展最佳实践文档中错误的 excludeTools 示例：此前示例使用完整命令字符串，永远无法匹配，因为排除规则仅与工具名称比对。填补了这一危险的文档缺口——此前用户误以为危险命令已被阻止。

  10. #29125 Convert hook timeout from seconds to milliseconds in hooks migration
    优先级 P2，核心领域，规模 S，已关闭
    修复 gemini hooks migrate 中的单位不匹配 bug：Claude Code 默认 60 秒的钩子超时被错误地解释为 Gemini CLI 中的 60 毫秒，导致迁移后的钩子立即超时。修复 #29122。

5. 热门讨论

本周期暂无讨论数据。

6. 功能需求趋势

  1. 代理自主性与能力扩展：用户强烈需求优化自定义技能/子代理的自动调用、在自主代理中集成原生 Google 搜索，以及支持 AST 感知的代码库导航，以减少 token 用量并提升精度。
  2. 增强浏览器代理健壮性：需求包括自动会话接管/锁定恢复、Wayland 兼容性，以及浏览器子代理正确继承设置。
  3. 持久、高效的会话管理：需求包括基于文件的持久化任务跟踪（替代上下文中的 WriteToDo）、跨会话持久化 /compress 状态，以及通过 /chat share 查看子代理执行轨迹。
  4. 沙箱与执行模型优化：用户对零依赖操作系统级沙箱感兴趣，以在维持安全边界的同时，利用 Gemini 3 原生的 bash/POSIX 工具适配能力。
  5. 记忆系统质量提升：需求包括确定性脱敏、修复低信号会话的无限重试问题，以及优化无效记忆补丁的错误处理。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. 子代理可靠性故障：用户普遍对子代理永久挂起、达到轮次限制后误报成功、无视用户配置、以及相关任务下无法被自主调用等问题感到不满。
  2. Shell 执行稳定性问题：反复有用户反馈 shell 命令执行完成后挂起，以及模型在目录中散落创建临时脚本，导致工作区杂乱。
  3. 自动记忆系统缺陷：存在多个相关 bug，包括静默失败、无限重试、脱敏前数据泄露，削弱了用户对记忆功能的信任。
  4. UI 与渲染故障：截断时拆分代理对导致表情符号丢失、UI 中子代理工具调用消失、终端调整大小闪烁等问题影响日常使用体验。
  5. 配置与迁移 bug：钩子迁移单位不匹配、事件键映射错误、设置无法传播到子代理等问题，给自定义配置的用户带来意外故障。
  6. 安全边缘场景：通过不可信构建文件的提示注入、NTFS 短名路径漏洞、记忆流程中机密脱敏薄弱等问题，给在不可信环境中运行 CLI 的用户带来风险。

1. 近7天亮点

本周 Copilot CLI 团队发布了 4 个预发布版本（v1.0.84-2 至 v1.0.84-5），核心更新包括编辑器中 Vim 模式正式可用、基于语法解析的 Shell 补全，以及用于语义化 JSONL 格式交互的会话/记忆导入命令。社区讨论主要围绕 MCP（模型上下文协议）兼容性缺陷、组织级 Agent 可见性不足，以及长时间运行会话中频繁出现的 OOM 崩溃等性能问题。安全与安装程序加固也取得进展：CI 工作流已固定依赖版本，未支持操作系统的检测逻辑也得到优化。

6. 功能请求趋势

根据开放 issue 和社区活动，最受关注的需求方向为：

  1. Vim/模态编辑体验深化 —— v1.0.84-2 中 Vim 模式正式发布后，社区提出自定义（如自定义快捷键、ex 命令）等后续需求
  2. 跨会话上下文与记忆 —— 要求支持跨会话的持久化、可查询上下文（见 #2436），以及官方的导入/导出工具
  3. 企业级 Agent 可发现性 —— 组织级与共享 Agent 的可见性、权限范围划分，以及集中化管理能力
  4. MCP 生态兼容性 —— 更严格的规范合规性、更好的错误处理，以及更广泛的第三方 MCP 服务器支持（Atlassian、FastMCP 等）
  5. Agent 可观测性 —— 后台子 Agent 的实时进度流式展示，以及对长时间运行的工具调用序列的更好可见性（见 #2254）

7. 开发者痛点

本周社区反馈的高频问题：

  • 内存不稳定：Linux 和 Windows 均有多个 OOM 崩溃报告，尤其是长时间/恢复的会话会触及 V8 堆内存 4 GB 上限
  • MCP 连接脆弱：超时回归、规范不合规、OAuth 回调不匹配，以及取消操作后工具被永久移除
  • Windows/WSL2 性能与兼容性问题：空闲时 CPU 占用过高、Windows 25H2 沙箱支持不足、插件更新与 VS Code 冲突，以及不明原因的原生运行时崩溃
  • 授权体验摩擦：单次请求提示次数过多，且会话运行约 1 小时后辅助权限功能会失效
  • 安装程序与环境缺陷：私有 Azure 源上的语音安装程序返回 401 错误、BSD 系统上操作系统检测错误，以及 v1.0.83 中无法加载工作区 .mcp.json 文件

#48846: fix(ai): sanitize assistant text for Claude requests 待合入 提升Claude/Bedrock Converse的可靠性：在分配缓存标记前省略空的助手文本块，并修剪助手前缀的尾部空白，以避免上游验证错误。
#48867: feat(core): make worktree APIs project-based 待合入 基于项目的工作树管理初步实现：所有工作树操作现在都需要projectID，而非任意路径。让多项目工作树工作流更安全。
#48878: fix(tui): force terminal reset on exit for Windows ConPTY 待合入 修复Windows终端退出时的损坏问题（修复#48776）：在ConPTY环境（例如Alacritty + zellij）中退出opencode时，强制执行完整的终端重置，此前该问题会导致Shell处于原始/损坏状态。
#47913: docs: add Indonesian translation (README.id.md) 待合入 社区贡献，新增完整的印尼语README翻译，扩大了OpenCode对印尼语开发者的覆盖范围（修复#47910）。

5. 热门讨论

已省略 — 数据集中未提供GitHub Discussions相关数据。

6. 功能请求趋势

  1. UI/UX控制与回退选项：用户反复请求增加布局切换按钮，以回退到旧版左侧边栏UI，同时恢复新UI重设计中移除的缺失控件（MCP开关）。
  2. 支付灵活性：OpenCode Go的加密货币支付支持是得票最高的新功能请求，主要由传统支付方式受限地区的用户推动。
  3. 会话管理增强：用户需求包括提升会话可靠性、卡死会话可恢复性，以及更智能的上下文压缩（例如后缀模式）以支持长时间运行的工作。
  4. v2子代理功能对齐：用户呼吁补齐v2缺失的子代理能力，包括对单体仓库的跨位置子代理支持，以及取消正在运行的后台子代理的功能。
  5. 插件生态扩展：开发者希望获得更广泛的插件API访问权限（会话列表、事件流、表单控件），以构建功能更强大的第三方集成。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. v1.18.30版本不稳定：最新稳定版存在严重回归问题，由于系统提示词组装时出现TypeError，会导致所有提示词崩溃，用户被迫降级到v1.18.20或v1.18.18。
  2. 剪贴板功能长期失效：复制到剪贴板功能已损坏超过10个月仍未修复，给依赖复制生成代码的用户带来日常困扰。
  3. 会话可靠性问题：重启后仍无法解除的会话卡死、 phantom 工具片段、非Git会话路径归属Bug，都会导致工作丢失和令人困惑的用户体验。
  4. 新UI缺少关键功能：重设计后的UI移除了用户熟悉的控件（MCP开关、布局切换）且没有替代方案，导致用户无法配置核心功能。
  5. TUI插件生态脆弱：由于OpenTUI双入口和双运行时回归问题，基于npm的TUI插件在最新版本中无法使用，目前只有临时回退方案。
  6. 平台特有缺陷：Windows用户持续面临独特的Bug：离线安装包损坏（缺少ripgrep）、退出时终端损坏、非Git会话路径问题，以及随机推理中断。
  7. v2.0多模态/工具调用不稳定：使用Muse Spark模型的Zen网关用户完全无法使用图片输入或工具调用功能，原因是上游授权错误。

Pi 社区周报 | 2026-09-14

1. 近 7 天亮点

本周 Pi 社区重点聚焦于 TUI 稳定性、模型提供商兼容性以及扩展生态的发展。本周暂无官方新版本发布，但核心可靠性修复、新增 OAuth 提供商支持，以及一大批基于 Pi RPC 模式构建的第三方 GUI/工具项目都在稳步推进。社区最关注的问题集中在 Codex 传输可靠性，以及大篇幅会话记录下的 TUI 渲染性能。

6. 功能需求趋势

  1. GUI / Web UI 生态扩张：大量基于 pi --mode rpc 构建的第三方桌面/网页客户端涌现，表明非 TUI 界面存在强烈的未被满足的需求，同时越来越多的声音呼吁推出官方 Web UI 基础框架，以规范扩展 UI 开发。

  3. 会话管理优化：分支删除、从恢复列表分叉会话、/new 会话间的持久化状态是反复出现的可用性需求。
  4. 更强的扩展能力：自定义 OAuth 页面渲染、工作指示器 UI 租约、权限门控钩子是扩展开发者的核心诉求。
  5. 代理可观测性工具：随着用户运行更复杂的自主工作流，上下文内存追踪、循环检测、长代理运行的工具调用分组等需求持续增长。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. Codex / OpenAI Responses 传输可靠性：#4945 卡顿问题及相关的 #9474 超时 Bug 是用户最主要的不满来源，频繁出现「Working...」卡死导致工作丢失的反馈。
  2. 大篇幅会话记录下的 TUI 性能：多个相互关联的问题（#8036、#9255、#9549）会导致在处理长对话历史或大 diff 时出现崩溃、重绘风暴和 CPU 核心占满。
  3. Windows 兼容性缺口：Shell 检测失败、应用商店别名问题、二进制文件解析不一致，让 Windows 用户的使用体验欠佳。
  4. 新工具链下的包/安装摩擦：pnpm 11 兼容性问题和 jiti 缓存权限问题导致现代开发环境下的安装失败。
  5. 自适应模型的边缘情况：压缩输出上限失败（#9075）和模型上下文窗口默认值错误（#9566）会影响使用前沿本地模型或自适应推理模型用户的工作流。
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code 社区周报 | 2026-09-14

1. 过去7天亮点

Qwen Code 项目发布了稳定版 CLI v0.23.3，推出功能扩展的桌面客户端 v0.3.0 预览版，并推进了多智能体沙箱和 Web Shell 远程连接能力的开发。TUI 中高优先级的 React #185 渲染崩溃问题引发了社区大量紧急 bug 反馈，安全加固与沙箱隔离也成为当前开发的核心优先级。

2. 版本发布

版本 类型 核心变更
v0.23.3 CLI 稳定版 为 Kimi、Qwen 和 DeepSeek 模型扩展了推理预设（#11349）；无破坏性变更

cua-driver-rs-v0.20.6 驱动更新 预构建 CUA 驱动二进制文件：含代码签名的 macOS 通用二进制、Linux x86_64/arm64 版本（glibc 2.31+）、Windows UIAccess 工作进程
sdk-typescript-v0.1.12 SDK 内置 CLI v0.23.3

3. 热门问题

  1. #11500 – 后台智能体并发完成时 TUI 静默崩溃（React #185）
    这是 P1 级 UI bug：当多个子智能体快速连续完成任务时，会触发未捕获的“Maximum update depth exceeded”错误，用户会被直接退回 shell 且无任何错误提示。该 issue 有 12 条评论，是当前讨论最多的活跃问题。
  2. #5199 – Windows 上反复出现 React #185 错误
    这是长期存在的开放 issue，本周有更新，共 8 条评论。反馈称在 Windows 的 Cherry Studio 安装环境中也出现了相同的渲染循环崩溃，说明该问题可跨环境复现。
  3. #11756 – 后台智能体工作流中虚拟化历史记录功能崩溃
    P1 级 bug，在 v0.23.3 稳定版上启用 Virtualized History 后可复现，由多智能体工作流更新会话历史触发。
  4. #11783 – 后台 shell 任务注册后 TUI 崩溃
    P1 级 UI 崩溃，在调用带 is_background: true 参数的 run_shell_command 数秒后发生，证实后台任务生命周期是核心崩溃诱因。
  5. #11764 – 安全问题：单引号内反斜杠可绕过 Bash 允许规则
    P1 级漏洞：当已保存的 Bash(...) 允许规则中，第一条命令以单引号包裹的反斜杠结尾时，会自动授权执行第二条未提示的命令，存在沙箱逃逸风险。
  6. #11695 – 追踪：将智能体框架与执行环境分离
    核心架构提案，旨在将智能体循环与工具执行进程解耦，实现可独立部署、可寻址的运行时沙箱。5 条评论表明维护者对这一路线图方向有强烈兴趣。
  7. #11704 – 提案：推出官方 Android 配套客户端
    功能请求：开发原生 Android 瘦客户端，通过 ACP 连接 qwen serve，提交者表示愿意开发并维护 MVP。5 条评论显示社区对移动端访问有较高需求。
  8. #11718 – 桌面端 AppImage Python 环境泄漏导致 MCP 服务器崩溃
    已关闭 bug：AppImage 打包的 PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH 会泄漏到派生的 stdio MCP 服务器中，导致外部 Python 解释器异常。本周经过 4 条评论讨论后已修复。
  9. #11590 – DashScope 网关元数据字段不匹配导致非 Qwen 模型调用失败
    已关闭 P1 级集成 bug：自动注入的 metadata 对象会导致第三方模型在 DashScope OpenAI 兼容端点上返回 400 错误。经社区反馈后已修复。
  10. #11762 – /delete 命令未清理 ~/.qwen/tmp/<hash>/logs.json
    隐私相关 bug：会话删除后完整会话日志仍会保留，且无设置项可禁用或限制日志累积，引发用户对数据留存的担忧。

4. 核心 PR 进展

  1. #11548 – feat(web-shell): 连接选定的远程守护进程
    支持独立 Web Shell 通过地址 + bearer token 连接指定的远程守护进程，可切换目标并复用现有工作区/会话/终端接口。
  2. #11614 – feat(cli): 为 Linux 新增 bwrap 内核沙箱后端
    新增基于内核级 bwrap 隔离的轻量级 Linux 沙箱，无需容器运行时/root 权限/守护进程。该功能为可选开启，保留原有 macOS 和容器后端。
  3. #11711 – feat(core): 为子智能体新增容器执行能力
    在 Unix 系统上为普通子智能体执行实现 Docker/Podman 容器后端，支持通过环境变量和智能体级配置标志强制启用容器化运行。
  4. #11206 – feat(mesh): 新增持久化共享线程智能体协作能力
    引入带共享线程协作的持久化工作区智能体身份，支持任务分配、插话、结果归因、单次运行历史记录、取消和审核工作流。
  5. #11692 – feat(core): 支持配置 web_search 预算并限制提取器降级逻辑
    可通过 tools.webSearch.timeoutMs 配置 web_search 超时时间（默认从 60 秒提升至 120 秒），并在搜索预算耗尽时限制模型输入。
  6. #11086 – feat(serve): 将扩展作用域限定为工作区运行时
    将全局扩展目录的作用域调整为按工作区运行时划分，实现扩展状态协调、带工作区限定的守护进程/SDK 访问，以及更新后的扩展管理 UI。
  7. #11280 – fix(skills): 会话恢复时重新应用 Skill 的副作用
    修复了恢复会话时仅还原指令、丢失运行时状态的问题，现在会从已加载的 Skill 中恢复 allowedTools 规则和 hooks。
  8. #11538 – feat: 支持按模型选择 OpenAI 通信 API
    为 OpenAI 兼容服务商新增按模型配置 wireApi 的功能（可选 chat-completions / responses），CLI、ACP、守护进程、Web Shell 和 VS Code 设置流程均已支持。
  9. #11242 – feat(browser-use): 新增 Chrome 原生消息中转
    通过原生消息 + Qwen Chrome 扩展将浏览器 SDK 连接到本地 Chrome，支持调试器挂载、CDP 命令转发，无需单独启动浏览器实例即可实现浏览器自动化。
  10. #11722 – feat(web-shell): 新增 PWA 安装支持与 Android 开发 shell
    为守护进程提供的 Web Shell 添加 PWA 元数据和生产环境 Service Worker，支持安装使用并提供 Android 开发 shell 体验，与移动端配套客户端提案对齐。

5. 热门讨论

本周数据集未提供讨论数据。

6. 功能请求趋势

  1. 沙箱与执行隔离：用户需求集中在内核级（bwrap）和容器级（Docker/Podman）子智能体隔离，以及将智能体框架与执行环境正式分离（#11695、#11614、#11711）。
  2. 移动端与远程访问：社区对官方 Android 客户端、通过 qwen serve 远程访问 Qwen Code 的 PWA 支持有强烈兴趣（#11704、#11722、#11548）。
  3. 多智能体协作：用户请求支持持久化智能体身份、共享线程工作区，以及跨守护进程和 Web Shell 的结构化后台任务追踪（#11206、#11636）。
  4. Web 搜索可配置性：需求包括可调整搜索超时时间和受限的降级行为，以提升可靠性并控制成本（#11687、#11692）。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. TUI 稳定性（React #185 崩溃）：由后台智能体、虚拟化历史、并发子智能体完成触发的“Maximum update depth exceeded”错误反复出现，导致静默崩溃和会话状态丢失（#11500、#5199、#11756、#11783）。
  2. CI 不稳定：共享运行器环境中间歇性出现测试失败、超时和 SIGTERM 终止，在无逻辑错误的情况下阻塞 PR 合并和发布流水线（#10490、#11777、#11736）。
  3. 内存泄漏与会话持久化问题：长时间运行的会话内存占用过高（最高达 7GB）、崩溃后无恢复路径、会话删除时日志数据清理不彻底（#11724、#11762）。
  4. 跨模型兼容性：通过 DashScope 网关使用非 Qwen 模型时，因无条件注入元数据字段导致静默失败（#11590）。
  5. 桌面环境泄漏：AppImage 打包的 Python 环境变量会泄漏到派生的 MCP 服务器，导致 Linux 上的外部 Python 工具异常（#11718）。

本周报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

AI CLI Tools Weekly Digest 2026-09-14

Generated: 2026-09-14 00:53 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool AI CLI Ecosystem Comparison Report | 2026-09-14

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI developer CLI ecosystem is entering a maturation phase defined by three parallel priorities: enterprise-grade reliability, extensible plugin/agent frameworks, and cross-platform parity for Windows environments. Across all major tools, subagent orchestration and sandboxed execution have shifted from experimental features to core infrastructure, with growing community demand for granular control over safety filters, cost tracking, and session state management. The market is also seeing a divergence between vendor-native tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI) focused on tight integration with their parent model ecosystems, and community-driven multi-provider tools (OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code) building interoperable, customizable agent platforms. Windows platform stability has emerged as a universal pain point, with every major tool reporting critical Windows-specific bugs spanning process lifecycle, shell integration, and sandbox functionality.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (Last 7 Days) PRs (Last 7 Days) Discussions (Last 7 Days) Release Status
Claude Code 10 tracked hot issues (8 open, 2 closed) 10 tracked PRs (7 merged, 3 open) N/A (no discussion data provided) 5 patch releases (v2.1.266–v2.1.270)
OpenAI Codex 10 tracked hot issues (all open) 10 tracked PRs (all open/active) 10 active discussions (4 ideas, 3 Q&A, 3 show-and-tell) 1 stable Python SDK release (v0.154.0), 7 Rust alpha builds
Gemini CLI 10 tracked hot issues (9 open, 1 closed) 10 tracked PRs (9 open, 1 merged) N/A (no discussion data provided) 1 preview release (v0.60.0-preview.0), 3 nightly builds (v0.61.0 line)
GitHub Copilot CLI 10 tracked hot issues (8 open, 2 closed) 10 tracked PRs (7 merged, 3 open) N/A (no discussion data provided) 4 pre-release builds (v1.0.84-2 through v1.0.84-5)
OpenCode 10 tracked hot issues (all open) 10 tracked PRs (all open) N/A (no discussion data provided) 1 stable release (v1.18.30) with critical regression
Pi 10 tracked hot issues (9 open, 1 closed) 10 tracked PRs (6 open, 4 merged) 9 active discussions (2 Q&A, 2 ideas, 5 show-and-tell) No new releases
Qwen Code 10 tracked hot issues (7 open, 3 closed) 10 tracked PRs (all open/active) N/A (no discussion data provided) 2 stable releases (CLI v0.23.3, Desktop v0.3.0), 4 nightly builds, 2 SDK/driver updates

3. Shared Feature Directions

  1. Advanced session state management

    • Tools: OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI
    • Needs: Native rewind/undo (Codex top-voted request), persistent session compression across restarts (Gemini CLI #21335), session tree branching and pruning (Pi #9531), and recoverable stuck sessions (OpenCode #43277). Users are moving beyond linear chat workflows and require version-control-like state management for long-running agent tasks.

  2. Plugin/agent ecosystem maturity

    • Tools: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Pi, OpenCode, Qwen Code
    • Needs: Standardized plugin testing frameworks (Claude Code claude plugin eval), expanded plugin API surfaces for session and event access (OpenCode #46690), MCP (Model Context Protocol) compliance and compatibility fixes (Copilot CLI #4809, Pi ecosystem tools), and skill-to-plugin conversion tooling (Codex community project).

  3. Cross-platform Windows parity

    • Tools: All 7 tools
    • Needs: Process lifecycle and orphaned lock fixes (Claude Code #42776, Codex #29079), shell integration and path handling (Claude Code #72728, Pi #9504), sandbox reliability (Codex #31073, Qwen Code bwrap backend), and offline installer robustness (OpenCode #34442). Windows users represent a large share of the user base but consistently report a degraded experience relative to macOS/Linux.

  4. Granular usage/cost transparency

    • Tools: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI
    • Needs: Accurate quota accounting for background processes (Codex #27773), context-overflow error clarification (Claude Code #61716), configurable web search budget controls (Qwen Code #11692), and usage tracking tools (Codex community Codex Limits tool).

  5. Sandbox & security hardening

    • Tools: Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Claude Code, Codex
    • Needs: Kernel-level sandbox isolation (Qwen Code bwrap backend), prompt injection mitigation for untrusted build files (Gemini CLI v0.61.0 nightly), NTFS path vulnerability fixes (Gemini CLI #29116), and Bash rule bypass prevention (Qwen Code #11764).

4. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension Claude Code OpenAI Codex Gemini CLI GitHub Copilot CLI OpenCode Pi Qwen Code
Core Focus Enterprise-grade plugin framework, safety guardrails, multi-provider support TUI UX polish, OpenAI model ecosystem integration, remote orchestration Agent reliability, security hardening, subagent autonomy GitHub ecosystem integration, enterprise admin, MCP compatibility Multi-provider flexibility, UI customization, plugin extensibility Multi-provider interoperability, RPC-based ecosystem expansion, performance optimization Self-hosted/on-prem use cases, multi-agent collaboration, sandbox isolation
Target Users Enterprise security teams, plugin developers, regulated industries General developers, OpenAI power users, ChatGPT ecosystem users Google Cloud users, security-focused teams, enterprise admins GitHub enterprise customers, DevOps teams, VS Code users Indie developers, power users, multi-model tinkerers TUI power users, extension developers, self-hosted community Chinese market users, on-prem deployments, multi-agent workflow teams
Technical Approach Modular plugin architecture with first-class mod framework; conservative release cadence with frequent patch fixes Rust-based core with iterative TUI improvements; tight coupling to OpenAI Responses API Security-first development with frequent nightly hardening; focus on subagent state correctness Node.js-based CLI aligned with GitHub platform APIs; enterprise-focused access controls TypeScript/JavaScript core with highly extensible plugin API; community-driven feature development Performance-optimized TUI with RPC API for third-party UIs; provider-agnostic abstraction layer Rust/C++ core with multi-backend sandboxing; built for Qwen models with multi-provider support
Release Cadence Weekly patch releases (5 in 7 days) Weekly stable + daily alpha builds Weekly preview + daily nightlies Weekly pre-release builds Irregular stable releases with community hotfixes Infrequent official releases with active PR development Multiple release tracks (stable CLI, desktop, nightly, SDKs)

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Highest Momentum

  • OpenAI Codex: Boasts the most active community discussion forum, with 10 tracked discussions spanning feature ideas, Q&A, and third-party tooling. The Awesome Codex CLI curated list (150+ ecosystem tools) and multiple community-built plugins indicate a thriving third-party ecosystem. Top issues receive 30+ upvotes and 50+ comments, reflecting high user engagement.
  • Claude Code: Shows strong contributor velocity with 5 patch releases in 7 days and active work on the plugin framework. The extension of issue lifecycles from 14 to 90 days signals a maturing project prioritizing community feedback. High-comment issues (182 comments on #42776) demonstrate a large, engaged user base.
  • Pi: Has a rapidly growing third-party GUI/tooling ecosystem built on its RPC mode, with 5+ community-built desktop/web clients shared in the last week. The project’s provider-agnostic approach is attracting extension developers, and core performance work (startup latency targeting jcode parity) indicates strategic investment in competitiveness.

Rapidly Iterating

  • Qwen Code: Ships updates across 6+ release tracks (CLI stable, nightly, desktop, SDK, driver) with active development on sandbox isolation, multi-agent collaboration, and mobile access. The project is rapidly expanding its feature set to compete with established Western tools.
  • Gemini CLI: Pushes daily nightly builds focused on security hardening and agent reliability, indicating fast-paced development as the tool catches up to competitors in subagent functionality.

Stability Challenges

  • OpenCode: The latest stable release (v1.18.30) has a critical regression crashing all prompts, and a 10-month-old clipboard bug remains unfixed, indicating quality control gaps. The project has high community engagement but slower issue resolution velocity.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI: In a pre-release phase (v1.0.84-x) with frequent builds but fewer community-contributed PRs, reflecting a more internally driven development model. Enterprise-focused features (org agents, MCP compatibility) are prioritized over community-requested UX polish.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Agent orchestration is becoming the core value proposition

    • Every tool is investing in subagent frameworks, background task execution, and multi-agent collaboration. The shift from "AI chat in the terminal" to "AI agent platform with worker orchestration" is accelerating, with users demanding features like cross-project subagents, persistent agent identities, and structured workflow delegation.
    • Developer takeaway: Build tooling around agent orchestration patterns, not just single-turn chat interfaces. Prioritize observability, cancellation, and state management for long-running agent tasks.

  2. MCP is emerging as the de facto extensibility standard

    • GitHub Copilot CLI, Pi, Claude Code, and Qwen Code are all investing in MCP compatibility, with community-driven MCP server ecosystems growing rapidly. Spec compliance issues (e.g., Copilot CLI #4809) are being prioritized as MCP becomes a baseline expectation for AI CLI tools.
    • Developer takeaway: Design plugins and integrations against the MCP specification to maximize cross-tool compatibility. Invest in MCP server tooling and testing frameworks.

  3. Windows is the next battleground for platform parity

    • With Windows-specific bugs dominating top issue lists across every tool, the first vendor to deliver a reliable, fully featured Windows experience will gain significant market share. Investments in Windows sandboxing, process lifecycle management, and shell integration are becoming competitive differentiators.
    • Developer takeaway: Allocate dedicated QA and engineering resources for Windows testing early in development. Use native Windows APIs (Job Objects, ConPTY) correctly to avoid common process lifecycle pitfalls.

  4. Safety filter tradeoffs are creating enterprise segmentation

    • Claude Code’s high volume of ClAudit false positives for security practitioners highlights a gap between one-size-fits-all safety filters and enterprise use cases. Tools that offer granular, domain-specific safety policy tuning and self-hosted filter options will capture security and regulated industry users.
    • Developer takeaway: Build safety systems with configurable policies and audit trails, not just binary allow/deny logic. Support domain-specific whitelisting for defensive security, DevOps, and admin use cases.

  5. Multi-provider, multi-model tools are gaining traction

    • Community-driven tools like Pi and OpenCode are attracting users who want flexibility across model providers, while vendor-native tools are adding cross-provider support (e.g., Claude Code’s max effort level capping across Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry). The ability to mix and match models for different tasks is becoming a key user requirement.
    • Developer takeaway: Design architectures with provider abstraction layers from the start. Support provider-specific features (e.g., thinking budgets, server-side tools) while maintaining consistent core behavior across backends.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills Community Highlights Report

Data as of 2026-09-14, sourced from anthropics/skills

1. Top Skills Ranking

Ranked by community engagement (comments/discussion volume, cross-referenced with linked issue activity):

Rank Skill / PR Functionality Discussion Highlights Status
1 PR #1298: skill-creator eval recall fix Fixes a critical bug where run_eval.py consistently reports 0% recall for all skill descriptions, breaking the entire skill description optimization loop; also resolves Windows stream reading errors, trigger detection issues, and parallel worker bugs. Tied to Issue #556 (12 comments, 7 👍), with 10+ independent user reproductions reported. The fix installs eval artifacts as real skills instead of temporary command files, and addresses cross-platform subprocess pipe failures. Open
2 PR #525: pyxel retro game development skill Adds a skill for the Pyxel retro game engine MCP server, enabling end-to-end pixel-art/8-bit game creation workflows (write → run → inspect → iterate) directly in Claude Code. One of the longest-running open new-skill PRs with consistent updates over 6+ months, indicating sustained community interest in creative/ game development use cases. Open
3 PR #514: document-typography skill Provides typographic quality control for AI-generated documents, preventing orphan word wrap, widow paragraphs, and numbering misalignment. Framed as a universal quality improvement for all Claude-generated document output, with broad cross-use-case applicability. Open
4 PR #1742: mcp-builder MCP 2.0 support Fixes mcp-builder compatibility with mcp>=2.0.0, including the renamed streamable_http_client import and custom HTTP header configuration via create_mcp_http_client. Resolves widely reported breakage (Issue #1668) for developers building MCP-backed skills following the MCP 2.0 protocol release. Open
5 PR #83: skill-quality + skill-security analyzer meta-skills Adds two meta-skills: a quality analyzer that evaluates skills across 5 dimensions (structure, functionality, trigger accuracy, etc.), and a security analyzer for risk auditing of custom skills. Aligns directly with top community security concerns (Issue #492, 43 comments), making it one of the most policy-relevant pending skill submissions. Open
6 PR #486: ODT document skill Enables creation, template filling, parsing, and HTML conversion of OpenDocument Format files (.odt, .ods). Fills a major gap in open-standard document support, complementing existing DOCX and PDF skills. Open
7 PR #1628: Hivemind multi-agent orchestration skill Lets Claude Code delegate mechanical work to headless opencode workers running on free models, with Claude retaining planner/reviewer/merger duties to reduce expensive model context usage. Addresses high demand for cost optimization in long-running agent workflows. Open
8 PR #541 + #539: docx + skill-creator bugfixes (Lubrsy706) Two complementary fixes: prevents DOCX tracked change ID collisions with existing bookmarks (stopping document corruption), and adds YAML special character validation for skill descriptions to prevent silent parsing failures. Represent high-impact reliability improvements for two of the most widely used core skills. Open (both)

2. Community Demand Trends

Distilled from top-voted and most-discussed Issues:

  1. Security & trust boundaries: The #1 most-discussed issue (#492, 43 comments) centers on community skills distributed under the anthropic/ namespace impersonating official tools, creating permission abuse risks. Users demand clear official/community labeling and security auditing tools.
  2. Enterprise collaboration: Org-wide skill sharing (#228, 16 comments, 8 👍) is the second-most requested feature, with users asking for internal shared skill libraries to replace manual .skill file distribution via chat tools.
  3. Skill development tooling reliability: Multiple high-comment bugs (#556, 12 comments, #1390) report broken evaluation pipelines for skill creators, including 0% trigger rates, silent serialization failures, and Windows incompatibility.
  4. Document workflow expansion: Users continue requesting expanded support for under-served document formats (ODT, advanced DOCX tracked changes, PDF case sensitivity fixes) and quality controls (typography, orphan comment detection).
  5. Agent efficiency & governance: Demand is growing for skills that reduce context window bloat (#1487: claude-api skill 156k token injection), enable multi-agent orchestration, and enforce output quality/reasoning gates (#1385).
  6. Platform compatibility: Users seek clearer guidance for using skills with alternative deployments like AWS Bedrock (#29) and standardization around MCP exposure for skills (#16).

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

Active PRs with clear use case demand, aligned with top community issues, and likely to land in the near term:

  • PR #1734: Orphaned DOCX comment detection: Adds auditing for unlinked/stray comments in DOCX files, complementing the existing robust DOCX skill suite and addressing document integrity user needs.
  • PR #1367: self-audit quality gate skill: Universal output auditing with mechanical file verification + four-dimension reasoning review, directly aligned with community demand for output reliability and governance tools.
  • PR #1627: Buffer API social scheduling skill: Cross-agent compatible skill for Buffer GraphQL API social media management, expanding the ecosystem into marketing/operations use cases.
  • PR #1615: scnet-hpc cluster skill: Profile-based SSH + Slurm workflow support for SCNet HPC clusters, filling a high-demand enterprise research computing gap.
  • PR #210: frontend-design skill improvement: Rewrite of the frontend-design skill for better actionability and token efficiency, addressing longstanding feedback about core skill clarity.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is for reliable, secure skill development infrastructure and trust safeguards — including fixed evaluation pipelines, clear official/community skill namespace separation, and security auditing tools — paired with expanded enterprise-grade capabilities for collaboration, document workflow, and cost-optimized agent orchestration.

Claude Code Community Digest | 2026-09-14

1. Last 7 Days' Highlights

Claude Code shipped 5 patch releases (v2.1.266–v2.1.270) over the past week, headlined by a new plugin evaluation framework, output-style switching controls, and cross-provider max effort level capping, alongside a critical regression fix for Bash git permission prompts. On the community side, Windows platform launch/stability bugs remain the most discussed open issues, while the project merged a wave of plugin/mod infrastructure updates and extended issue lifecycle windows to 90 days to reduce friction for contributors.

2. Releases

Version Key Changes
v2.1.270 Fixed regression from 2.1.269 where read-only git commands in Bash unexpectedly prompted for permission after long-running sessions.
v2.1.269 Added claude plugin eval for running reproducible plugin test suites with scored JSON/HTML reports; added /output-style [name] command to list/switch output styles across Remote Control, cloud, and OT environments.
v2.1.268 Added Claude apps gateway pricing sync: signed-in clients get matching rates via managed settings so /cost and telemetry align with the spend meter; added startup warning for gateways with empty access_control.allow_cidrs.
v2.1.267 Added maxEffortLevel setting (global or per-model) to cap effort across all providers (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry); added --system-prompt-snapshot off flag to render fresh system prompts on every request.
v2.1.266 Fixed 2.1.265 regression breaking LLM-gateway/proxy setups, where CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY incorrectly forced Cloud-gateway sign-in on its own.
v2.1.265 Added user.email and user.groups to telemetry from Claude Desktop/Cowork via apps gateways (matching terminal sessions); added support for --plugin-dir pointing to a folder of plugins with dynamic load/unload.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #42776: Claude Code Desktop fails to relaunch on Windows due to orphaned process file lock
    The highest-comment open issue (182 comments, 88 👍), this long-running Windows bug blocks app restarts after crashes and requires manual process cleanup. It has persisted since April 2026 and is the top pain point for desktop users.

  2. #53247: Claude Desktop fails to launch on Windows — orphaned Silo / Job Object after crash
    A related Windows stability issue (79 comments, 31 👍) with HRESULT 0x80070020 errors that only resolve via logoff or reboot. It highlights systemic gaps in Windows process lifecycle handling for the desktop app.

  3. #85371: ClAudit false-positive on screenshot image reference
    One of ~20 recently closed ClAudit false-positive reports from user sworrl, all triggering session-halts for legitimate defensive security, forensics, and general dev work. It underscores over-aggressive safety filtering for security practitioners.

  4. #85434: Safeguards trigger on local storage breakdown UI and redundancy coding
    A cyber-domain false positive blocking standard storage system engineering work, part of a pattern where defensive hardening tasks are misclassified as malicious.

  5. #85381: ClAudit false-positive on AD operations skill system prompt
    A cloud-IAM domain false positive that halted work on authorized Active Directory operations tooling, representing the risk of overblocking for enterprise admin use cases.

  6. #85372: ClAudit false-positive on NPM audit request
    A malware-forensics domain false positive triggered by a standard NPM audit task, showing that common dependency security scans can trip safety filters.

  7. #85365: ClAudit false-positive on SSH/UDR skill reference
    A crypto-secrets domain false positive from referencing SSH access in skill documentation, reflecting sensitivity around credential-related language even in defensive contexts.

  8. #85354: AUP false-positive on MySQL installation error discussion
    A usage-policy false positive (flagged by Fable 5) for a routine MySQL install troubleshooting request, showing AUP filters also misclassify standard devops work.

  9. #72728: Windows Git Bash shell-snapshot embeds raw Windows PATH, breaking command resolution
    An open Windows/Git Bash integration bug (4 comments, 1 👍) where unconverted Windows PATH values break short-name command lookups, adding to the list of Windows-specific shell compatibility issues.

  10. #85359: AUP false-positive on CT web hardening task
    A defensive-hardening domain AUP false positive where applying security best practices was incorrectly flagged, further demonstrating the overlap between legitimate security work and policy filter triggers.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #93215: Add mods: sec-default, diff and telemetry
    Published three built-in hooks-module plugins as source (sec-default, diff, telemetry) under the new mods/ directory, marking a major step toward open, extensible plugin architecture for core features.

  2. #93912: Unit tests for diff, sec-default and telemetry mods, typed against plugin declarations
    Introduced in-place unit testing for mods via claude plugin test, with type checking against official plugin declarations, improving testability and type safety for third-party plugin development.

  3. #93951: Move diff, sec-default and telemetry tests next to the mods
    Relocated mod test files to sit alongside each mod under mods/<mod>/tests/, aligning with standard plugin project structure and making it easier for contributors to work on individual mods.

  4. #93452: mods/diff: match the built-in /diff panel
    Aligned the diff mod’s UI with the built-in /diff panel (hunk rendering, controls, responsive behavior), ensuring feature parity between the native and plugin-based diff experiences.

  5. #89404: validate-agent.sh: don't abort at first warning, stop false-flagging valid agents
    Fixes the plugin-dev skill’s validation script, which failed on valid agent files due to set -euo pipefail edge cases, removing a major friction point for plugin developers.

  6. #79148: Add mandatory hookify. prefix to example rule filenames
    Fixes silent failures in hookify example rules that lacked the required filename prefix, correcting documentation drift and improving out-of-the-box rule functionality.

  7. #63686: Bump stale and autoclose timeouts from 14 to 90 days
    Extends issue lifecycle windows from 14 to 90 days, reducing noise from premature stale/closed labels and giving community issues more time to be triaged and addressed.

  8. #26175: Fix broken native installer bootstrap script
    Fixes the curl | bash install flow which silently failed to create the ~/.local/bin/claude binary and deleted existing npm installs, leaving users with no working CLI.

  9. #42205: fix(hookify): normalize tool matcher parsing
    Trims and normalizes hookify tool matcher strings, fixing match failures when separators had surrounding whitespace and improving the robustness of rule matching.

  10. #61716: Add troubleshooting for false usage limit caused by context overflow
    Documents a common misleading error where context overflow is misreported as a usage limit, and adds workaround guidance, addressing a frequent user confusion point.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data provided; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. Improved plugin/mod development tooling: The surge in mod framework PRs and plugin validation fixes aligns with growing demand for more robust, well-documented plugin build, test, and distribution tools.
  2. Granular safety/AUP filter controls: The high volume of ClAudit false-positive reports from security practitioners points to demand for whitelisting, domain-specific filter tuning, or self-hosted filter policy customization.
  3. Better cost and usage transparency: Gateway pricing sync and the context-overflow usage limit doc fix reflect demand for more accurate, explainable cost tracking and usage metering.
  4. Cross-platform parity for Windows: Persistent Windows desktop launch, process, and shell integration bugs indicate demand for prioritized Windows platform quality and testing.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Windows platform instability: Orphaned process locks, job object leaks, and Git Bash PATH issues make the Windows desktop and shell experience unreliable, with workarounds requiring reboots or manual process cleanup.
  2. Over-aggressive safety filtering for security work: Defensive security, forensics, and admin tasks routinely trigger false-positive session halts, disrupting legitimate work and creating friction for security-focused users.
  3. Plugin development rough edges: Silent rule failures, broken validation scripts, and inconsistent documentation create barriers to building and debugging custom plugins and hooks.
  4. Misleading error messages: Context overflow misreported as usage limits and silent install failures cause unnecessary confusion and debug time for end users.
  5. Short issue lifecycle windows: The previous 14-day stale/autoclose window was too aggressive, leading to valid community issues being closed before they could be triaged.
OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest | 2026-09-14

1. Last 7 Days' Highlights

This week saw the stable release of Python SDK 0.154.0 with new max and ultra reasoning-effort tiers, alongside a flurry of Rust alpha builds (v0.155.0-alpha.3.x line) focused heavily on Windows sandbox reliability. The community rallied around quality-of-life fixes for the TUI (notably removing the divisive Astra sparkle animation) and raised persistent concerns about Windows platform bugs, quota drainage, and missing core features like session rewind.

Stable Release

Alpha & CI Releases

  • Rust SDK: 7 pre-release builds in the v0.155.0-alpha.3.x line (through alpha.3.10) plus v0.154.0-alpha.6.2, focused on sandbox and platform hardening.

  1. Session state control: Native rewind/undo and per-PR persistent sessions are the most requested workflow features.

  3. Memory & context: Cross-session memories with source citation, plus better long-horizon context management transparency.

7. Developer Pain Points

  2. Quota opacity and drainage: Users report unexplained rapid usage burn, silent background quota consumption from processes like Codex Chronicle, and unclear reset policies.

  4. API-key auth limitations: Browser control, "Approve for me" permissions, and other features are unsupported under API-key authentication, fragmenting functionality.
  5. Missing basic editing primitives: No native rewind/revert forces users to rely on Git commits for every change, slowing iteration.
Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli

Gemini CLI Community Digest | 2026-09-14

1. Last 7 Days' Highlights

This week saw the rollout of the v0.60.0-preview.0 release and daily v0.61.0 nightly builds, with a heavy focus on security hardening (sandbox isolation, prompt injection mitigation, NTFS path safety) and agent reliability. Community-reported issues centered heavily on subagent execution bugs (hanging, incorrect success reporting, configuration ignore) and Auto Memory system defects, while open PRs targeted UI rendering fixes, A2A server stability, and core tool call robustness.

2. Releases

Version Type Key Changes
v0.61.0-nightly.20260913.g9c1b0a610 Nightly Full changelog available; incremental update from prior nightly
v0.61.0-nightly.20260912.g9c1b0a610 Nightly - Fix indirect prompt injection via build file modifications and untrusted flags (#29250)
- Harden sandbox filesystem boundaries and isolate runtime state
v0.61.0-nightly.20260909.ged2ac40df Nightly - Mitigate NTFS 8.3 short name (SFN) path vulnerabilities (#29116)
- Isolate settings directory in sandbox containers (#29216)
v0.60.0-preview.0 Preview - Improve destination validation and connection routing in web fetch utilities (#29120)
- Enforce RFC 9207 issuer identification in MCP OAuth flow
v0.59.0 Stable Version bump from nightly track; cumulative stability updates

3. Hot Issues

  1. #22323 Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS reports GOAL success
    P1 bug, 13 comments, 2 👍
    The codebase_investigator subagent falsely returns status: success with Termination Reason: GOAL even when it hits the maximum turn limit without completing analysis. This misleads users about task completion and is the most actively discussed issue this week.

  2. #21409 Generalist agent hangs indefinitely
    P1 bug, 8 comments, 8 👍 (top upvoted)
    Simple tasks (e.g., folder creation) hang forever when deferred to the generalist agent; disabling subagents resolves it. High community impact due to basic functionality failure, with the highest user upvote count this week.

  3. #19873 Zero-Dependency OS Sandboxing & Post-Execution Intent Routing
    P2 enhancement, 9 comments, 1 👍
    Proposes leveraging Gemini 3's native bash affinity by using POSIX toolchains via zero-dependency OS sandboxing, balancing the model's preferred workflow with security. Core architectural discussion for future agent execution.

  4. #25166 Shell command execution stuck on "Waiting input" after completion
    P1 core bug, 4 comments, 3 👍
    Simple shell commands hang with "Awaiting user input" even after finishing. A critical reliability issue for core shell execution functionality.

  5. #22745 Assess AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping
    P2 feature epic, 7 comments, 1 👍
    Tracks investigation into AST-aware tools for precise method-bound reads, reduced token noise, and faster codebase navigation. Key potential upgrade for codebase analysis performance.

  6. #26525 Add deterministic redaction and reduce Auto Memory logging
    P2 security bug, 5 comments
    Auto Memory sends transcript content to the model before secret redaction, risking sensitive data exposure in model context and logs. Important security and privacy gap.

  7. #21968 Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents autonomously
    P2 agent bug, 6 comments
    Users report the model never invokes custom skills/sub-agents on its own, even for highly relevant tasks (e.g., gradle/git operations), requiring explicit instruction. Degrades the utility of custom agent ecosystems.

  8. #26522 Stop Auto Memory from retrying low-signal sessions indefinitely
    P2 agent bug, 4 comments
    Low-signal sessions that the extraction agent skips remain marked unprocessed and are repeatedly re-surfaced, wasting cycles and degrading memory system efficiency.

  9. #22267 Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (maxTurns, etc.)
    P2 agent bug, 3 comments
    The browser subagent disregards global/project settings.json configurations like maxTurns, despite the AgentRegistry correctly merging settings. Breaks user configuration expectations for specialized agents.

  10. #21335 /compress command not persistent across session resume
    P2 agent bug, 2 comments, 2 👍
    Chat summaries from /compress are only stored in memory and not written to disk, so the compression is lost when the session is resumed. Users lose token savings across sessions.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #29286 Implement Google search tool in RobustAutonomousAgent
    Priority P1, size M, open
    Adds native Google search capability to the RobustAutonomousAgent, enabling real-time web lookups to supplement codebase and general knowledge tasks.

  2. #29163 Fix crash during authentication in git repositories
    Priority P1, area security, size L, open
    Prevents startup crashes when running Gemini CLI inside Git repositories under macOS Seatbelt or restricted permission environments, caused by the useGitBranchName hook failing to access .git directories.

  3. #29319 Guard JSON.parse on tool-call args in sendStream
    Priority P2, area non-interactive, size M, open
    Fixes stream termination from malformed tool call JSON by wrapping JSON.parse in try/catch, pushing a _parseError arg and continuing the stream instead of crashing. Fixes #29308.

  4. #29320 Register express.json before A2A routes so req.body is parsed
    Priority P2, area agent, size S, open
    Fixes broken JSON-RPC parsing for A2A server routes by moving express.json() middleware before route setup, ensuring req.body is populated for A2A endpoints. Fixes #29315.

  5. #27863 Prioritize structured display titles in tool invocation
    Priority P1, area non-interactive, size S, open, help wanted
    Updates getDisplayTitle() to prioritize _toolDisplayName over raw tool names, improving UI clarity for custom tools with user-friendly labels. Fixes #23018.

  6. #27754 Add missing return after 501 response in GET /tasks/metadata
    Priority P1, area core, size XS, open, help wanted
    Fixes an A2A server crash (ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT) caused by missing return after a 501 response, which let execution fall through to additional response logic. Fixes #21729.

  7. #29304 Avoid splitting surrogate pairs during truncation
    Area core, size S, open
    Fixes sanitizeForDisplay to preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs (e.g., emojis) during text truncation, preventing silent character drops when cutoffs land in the middle of multi-code-unit glyphs.

  8. #29208 Fall back to empty on malformed agents.json shape
    Priority P2, area agent, size S/M, open
    Gracefully handles corrupt agents.json (invalid shape from interrupted saves, sync conflicts, etc.) by falling back to empty state instead of crashing with TypeError or silently dropping acknowledgments. Fixes #29207.

  9. #28963 Correct excludeTools examples that never match
    Docs, size S, open
    Fixes incorrect excludeTools examples in extension best practices docs: the previous examples used full command strings which never match, since exclusions compare only against tool names. Resolves a dangerous documentation gap that left users thinking dangerous commands were blocked.

  10. #29125 Convert hook timeout from seconds to milliseconds in hooks migration
    Priority P2, area core, size S, closed
    Fixes a unit mismatch bug in gemini hooks migrate where Claude Code's 60-second default hook timeout was incorrectly interpreted as 60ms in Gemini CLI, causing migrated hooks to timeout immediately. Fixes #29122.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. Agent autonomy and capability expansion: Strong demand for better automatic use of custom skills/sub-agents, native Google search integration in autonomous agents, and AST-aware codebase navigation to reduce token usage and improve precision.
  2. Enhanced browser agent robustness: Requests for automatic session takeover/lock recovery, Wayland compatibility, and proper settings inheritance for the browser subagent.
  3. Persistent, efficient session management: Demand for file-based persistent task tracking (replacing in-context WriteToDo), persistent /compress state across sessions, and subagent trajectory visibility via /chat share.
  4. Sandbox and execution model optimization: Interest in zero-dependency OS-level sandboxing to leverage Gemini 3's native bash/POSIX tool affinity while maintaining security boundaries.
  5. Memory system quality improvements: Requests for deterministic redaction, infinite retry fixes for low-signal sessions, and better error handling for invalid memory patches.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Subagent reliability failures: Widespread frustration with subagents hanging indefinitely, falsely reporting success after hitting turn limits, ignoring user configuration, and not being invoked autonomously for relevant tasks.
  2. Shell execution stability issues: Recurring reports of shell commands hanging after completion, and the model creating scattered temporary scripts across directories that clutter workspaces.
  3. Auto Memory system defects: Multiple related bugs around silent failures, infinite retries, and pre-redaction data exposure that undermine trust in the memory feature.
  4. UI and rendering glitches: Surrogate pair splitting truncating emojis, disappearing subagent tool calls in the UI, and terminal resize flicker impact day-to-day user experience.
  5. Configuration and migration bugs: Hook migration unit mismatches, incorrect event key mapping, and settings that don't propagate to subagents create unexpected breakage for users customizing their setup.
  6. Security edge cases: Prompt injection via untrusted build files, NTFS short name path vulnerabilities, and weak secret redaction in memory flows create risk for users running the CLI in untrusted environments.

PR Status Description
#48770: refactor(codemode): materialize interpreter failures once at call boundary Open Rewrites interpreter error handling: failures travel as a single PendingThrow and become one Error object at the call site, not in built-in code. Eliminates misleading AST node attribution in built-in errors.
#46690: feat(plugin): expose session forms, session list, and global event stream Open Major plugin API expansion for v2: grants plugins access to session forms, full session listing, and the global event bus. Unlocks use cases like custom external UIs (e.g., Telegram bot integrations).
#44264: feat(session): add suffix compaction Open Adds experimental compaction.mode: "suffix" to session runtime and config. Preserves recent context while compacting older history, addressing long context window overflow issues for long-running sessions.
#48871: fix(project): resolve associated directory to its project instead of global Open Fixes non-git project session attribution: Project.resolve now checks the project_directory table before falling back to global ID, so sessions in non-git project roots are correctly associated (closes #48870).
#48862: fix(ai): preserve OpenAI Chat image URLs Open Fixes multimodal handling: HTTP/HTTPS image URLs are no longer incorrectly treated as base64 bytes in OpenAI Chat requests. Applies to both user-uploaded images and tool-returned remote images.
#44535: fix(session): stop creating phantom "unknown" tool parts on re-emitted deltas Open Fixes a long-standing bug (#33618) where opencode itself generated phantom unknown tool call parts during delta re-emission, not the upstream model.
#48846: fix(ai): sanitize assistant text for Claude requests Open Improves Claude/Bedrock Converse reliability: omits empty assistant text blocks before cache marker allocation and trims trailing whitespace from assistant prefixes to avoid upstream validation errors.
#48867: feat(core): make worktree APIs project-based Open First pass at project-based worktree management: all worktree operations now require a projectID instead of arbitrary locations. Enables safer multi-project worktree workflows.
#48878: fix(tui): force terminal reset on exit for Windows ConPTY Open Fixes Windows terminal corruption on exit (closes #48776): forces a full terminal reset when exiting opencode on ConPTY stacks (e.g., Alacritty + zellij), which previously left the shell in a raw/broken state.
#47913: docs: add Indonesian translation (README.id.md) Open Community contribution adding full Indonesian README translation, expanding OpenCode's accessibility to Indonesian-speaking developers (closes #47910).

5. Hot Discussions

Omitted — no GitHub Discussions data was provided in the dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. UI/UX control & rollback options: Users are repeatedly requesting a layout toggle to revert to the legacy left-sidebar UI, plus restoration of missing controls (MCP toggle) removed in the new UI redesign.
  2. Payment flexibility: Crypto payment support for OpenCode Go is the highest-voted new feature request, driven by users in regions with limited traditional payment access.
  3. Session management enhancements: Demand for better session reliability, recoverability for stuck sessions, and smarter context compaction (e.g., suffix mode) to support long-running work.
  4. v2 subagent feature parity: Users are pushing for missing v2 subagent capabilities, including cross-location subagent support for monorepos and cancellation of running background subagents.
  5. Plugin ecosystem expansion: Developers want broader plugin API surface access (session lists, event streams, form controls) to build more powerful third-party integrations.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. v1.18.30 release instability: The latest stable release has a critical regression that crashes all prompts due to a TypeError in system prompt assembly, forcing users to downgrade to v1.18.20/v1.18.18.
  2. Persistent clipboard functionality gap: The copy-to-clipboard feature has been broken for over 10 months with no fix, creating daily friction for users who rely on copying generated code.
  3. Session reliability issues: Stuck sessions that survive reboots, phantom tool parts, and non-git session attribution bugs cause lost work and confusing UX.
  4. New UI missing critical functionality: The redesigned UI removed familiar controls (MCP toggle, layout switch) with no replacement, leaving users unable to configure core features.
  5. TUI plugin ecosystem fragility: npm-based TUI plugins are broken on recent releases due to OpenTUI dual-entry and dual-runtime regressions, with only a temporary revert in place.
  6. Platform-specific gaps: Windows users face consistent unique bugs: offline installer breakage (missing ripgrep), terminal corruption on exit, non-git session path issues, and random inference interruptions.
  7. v2.0 multimodal/tool-use instability: Zen gateway users on Muse Spark models cannot use image input or tool calls at all due to upstream authorization errors.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest | 2026-09-14

Repository: earendil-works/pi

1. Last 7 Days' Highlights

This week the Pi community focused heavily on TUI stability, model provider compatibility, and extension ecosystem growth. No new official releases shipped, but active work advanced core reliability fixes, new OAuth provider support, and a wave of third-party GUI/tooling projects built on Pi's RPC mode. Top community concerns centered on Codex transport reliability and TUI rendering performance with large transcripts.

2. Releases

No new releases were published in the last 7 days.

3. Hot Issues

# Issue Why it matters Community reaction
1 #4945 openai-codex Connection Reliability Issues Long-running high-priority bug: GPT-5.5/Codex streams hang the TUI on "Working..." with no error, forcing users to abort turns. Core reliability blocker for Codex users. 78 comments, 33 👍 — most discussed issue this week, active debugging in progress.
2 #7739 Set a startup-time budget targeting jcode-comparable latency and memory Defines a performance baseline to close the startup latency/memory gap with jcode, a key competitive benchmark. 8 comments — early scoping phase, benchmark data shared.
3 #8036 Edit tool crashes TUI when rendering a large diff during execution and session resume Critical TUI crash triggered by ~14.5MB diffs from long-line HTML files, also breaking session resume. 8 comments — reproducible, impact confirmed by multiple users.
4 #9311 Fullscreen mouse selection survives session switch Minor but common TUI UX bug: text selection persists across session switches in fullscreen mode. 6 comments — clear fix identified, low effort high impact.
5 #5372 Allow custom OAuth callback page rendering Unblocks custom branding for OAuth flows in embedded/white-label Pi deployments. 5 comments — requested by enterprise/extension developers.
6 #9255 TuiMainScreen: full-screen redraw storm when changed rows sit above the viewport top Major performance issue on long transcripts: violent jumping/doubled text from unnecessary full redraws every frame during streaming. 4 comments — root cause identified, affects all heavy users.
7 #9075 Compaction summarisation inherits session thinking level on adaptive models and deterministically hits output cap at high efforts Compaction fails on high-effort adaptive Anthropic models, as thinking tokens eat into the fixed output budget. 3 comments, 3 👍 — impacts advanced users of Claude adaptive thinking.
8 #9474 Codex transport: no non-resetting per-request total deadline; periodic events defeat idle timeout Related to #4945: stalled streams with keepalive events never time out, contributing to the "Working..." hang. 3 comments — part of the ongoing Codex reliability work.
9 #9566 context size defaults to 128k despite the real size being available Bug where matching model IDs in models.json override correct context window/cost data with defaults, breaking local LLM setups. 2 comments — closed quickly with fix applied.
10 #9567 pi install fails with pnpm >= 11 (blockExoticSubdeps on by default) Installation failure on latest pnpm due to URL-pinned subdependency in pi-mcp-adapter. 1 comment — affects all pnpm 11 users, high priority for package maintainers.

4. Key PR Progress

# PR Description
1 #9548 Mid conversation system messages Open — Core architectural change: system prompt/tool changes are recorded in the transcript instead of silently rewriting session state, enabling correct branch navigation and resume of modified sessions.
2 #9488 fix(ai): add canonical Codex turn attribution Open — Adds provider-neutral request identity metadata to Codex streams, enabling reliable attribution across tool continuations, retries, and compaction recovery (supports #4945 debugging).
3 #9096 feat(ai,coding-agent): add Meta provider with Muse subscription OAuth Open — Adds Meta Muse as a native provider with subscription OAuth login (no API key required).
4 #9504 fix(coding-agent): accept Windows Store shell aliases Open — Fixes Windows shell detection to work with Store-installed aliases (e.g. winget, powershell) that fail existsSync() checks.
5 #9501 fix(coding-agent): resolve Windows shells from installation directories Open — Unifies Windows binary discovery logic, greatly improving compatibility with non-standard shell installations on Windows.
6 #8635 fix(ai): preserve aborted stop reason during lazy setup Open — Fixes abort signal handling during lazy stream setup, correctly reporting aborted requests instead of generic setup failures.
7 #9531 feat(tree): add permanent branch deletion from session tree Closed — Implements permanent session tree branch pruning via Shift+D in the /tree selector, with protections for active paths and proper compaction re-pointing.
8 #9556 feat(ai): serverTools — declare provider server-side tools in model config Closed — Adds support for declaring provider-built server-side tools (e.g. OpenAI Responses web_search, Zhipu GLM search) in model configuration.
9 #9529 feat(ai): add Google Antigravity and Cursor Pro OAuth providers Closed — Adds two new subscription OAuth providers: Google Antigravity (Cloud Code Assist) and Cursor Pro, no API keys required.
10 #9517 feat(tui): group long tool-call runs Closed — Collapses 6+ consecutive tool calls into an aggregate transcript row with expand/collapse interaction, reducing clutter from long agent execution loops.

5. Hot Discussions

Q&A

  1. #3373 Which plugins, add-ons, or extensions do you most enjoy using with the Pi agent?

    • Long-running community thread with 16 comments / 9 👍: users share their favorite extensions and tooling built on Pi.

  2. #9516 openai-responses: tool-result images in function_call_output dropped by compatible gateways

    • Technical discussion about Responses API image encoding compatibility issues with third-party gateways.

Ideas

  1. #8420 From the DSH plugin ecosystem to pi: are we missing an official Web UI base?

    • 2 👍: Discussion comparing Pi's extension ecosystem to DSH's plugin scene, asking if Pi should ship an official Web UI base to unlock more UI-focused community contributions.

  2. #8803 Introducing pi-verdict — a minimal permission gate for pi: allow / ask / deny, one file, zero dependencies

    • 1 👍: Proposal/demo of a lightweight permission gate extension that adds per-tool-call approval, in the style of Claude Code's auto mode.

Show and tell

  1. #9552 Show & tell: Pi Heao GUI — a Windows desktop client for pi (built on the pi-agent-studio chat UI)

    • New Windows desktop GUI for Pi that reuses the official pi-agent-studio chat UI instead of reimplementing it.

  2. #9525 Thank you — --mode rpc is the backbone of a new open-source project

    • Community member shares web-agent, a phone-friendly web dashboard + Siri/Matrix bridge built on top of Pi's RPC mode with a persistent session.

  3. #9446 Phosphor – a desktop surface for pi

    • Desktop app that runs Pi sessions side-by-side with diffs, files, terminal, and artifacts, supporting all Pi providers plus Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT.

  4. #9427 Pi Manager — a local UI for providers, models, and writing ~/.pi/agent

    • Local control plane UI for managing providers, model catalogs, and ~/.pi/agent configuration without editing files manually.

  5. #9373 pi-agent-views — concurrent sub-agents, rendered by pi itself

    • Extension implementing Claude Code-style agent views: run multiple concurrent sub-agents with different models, switchable via hotkey.

  6. #9327 Eco Coding — a GUI for Pi (vision split, teams, browser, computer use + mobile)

    • Open-source desktop GUI for Pi with vision split, team features, browser integration, and mobile support.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. GUI / Web UI ecosystem expansion: An explosion of third-party desktop/web clients built on pi --mode rpc signals strong unmet demand for non-TUI interfaces, plus a growing call for an official Web UI base to standardize extension UI development.
  2. More subscription OAuth providers (no API keys): Repeated requests for native support for paid AI services with browser OAuth login (Meta Muse, Google Antigravity, Cursor Pro) instead of manual API key configuration.
  3. Session management improvements: Branch deletion, session forking from resume lists, and persistent state across /new sessions are recurring usability requests.
  4. Enhanced extension capabilities: Custom OAuth page rendering, working-indicator UI leases, and permission gate hooks are top asks for extension developers.
  5. Tooling for agent observability: Context memory tracing, loop detection, and tool-call grouping for long agent runs are growing requests as users run more complex autonomous workflows.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Codex / OpenAI Responses transport reliability: The #4945 hang issue and related #9474 timeout bug are the single biggest source of user frustration, with frequent reports of lost work from stuck "Working..." states.
  2. TUI performance on large transcripts: Multiple overlapping issues (#8036, #9255, #9549) cause crashes, redraw storms, and saturated CPU cores when working with long conversation history or large diffs.
  3. Windows compatibility gaps: Shell detection failures, Store alias issues, and inconsistent binary resolution create a rough experience for Windows users.
  4. Package/install friction with newer tooling: pnpm 11 compatibility breaks and jiti cache permission issues cause setup failures on modern development environments.
  5. Adaptive model edge cases: Compaction output cap failures (#9075) and incorrect model context window defaults (#9566) break workflows for users running cutting-edge local or adaptive-thinking models.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest | 2026-09-14

1. Last 7 Days' Highlights

The Qwen Code project shipped the stable v0.23.3 CLI release, expanded desktop client capabilities with a v0.3.0 preview, and advanced multi-agent sandboxing and Web Shell remote connectivity. A cluster of high-priority React #185 rendering crashes in the TUI drove urgent community bug reports, while security hardening and sandbox isolation emerged as top development priorities.

2. Releases

Release Type Key Changes
v0.23.3 Stable CLI Expanded reasoning presets for Kimi, Qwen, and DeepSeek models (#11349); no breaking changes
desktop-v0.3.0-preview.0 Desktop Preview Pre-release build with scheduled packaging CI (#11519); bridge permission state fixes
desktop-v0.3.0 Desktop Stable Official desktop release with improved bridge handling
v0.23.3-nightly builds (20260910–20260913) Nightly DingTalk background response aggregation refactor (#11570); channel API breaking changes
cua-driver-rs-v0.20.6 Driver Update Prebuilt CUA driver binaries: codesigned macOS universal binary, Linux x86_64/arm64 (glibc 2.31+), Windows UIAccess worker
sdk-typescript-v0.1.12 SDK Bundles CLI v0.23.3
v0.23.2 Stable CLI Improved split-view session navigation for web-shell (#11250); no breaking changes

3. Hot Issues

  1. #11500 – TUI silent crash (React #185) on concurrent background agent completion
    P1 UI bug causing uncaught "Maximum update depth exceeded" errors when multiple subagents finish in quick succession, dropping users back to the shell with no error context. 12 comments make it the most-discussed active issue.
  2. #5199 – Recurring React error #185 on Windows
    Long-running open issue with 8 comments, updated this week, reporting the same render loop crash on Windows Cherry Studio installations, indicating cross-environment reproducibility.
  3. #11756 – Virtualized history crash during background-agent workflows
    P1 bug reproducible on v0.23.3 stable with Virtualized History enabled, triggered by multi-agent workflows updating conversation history.
  4. #11783 – TUI crash after background shell task registration
    P1 UI crash occurring seconds after run_shell_command with is_background: true is invoked, confirming background task lifecycle as a core crash vector.
  5. #11764 – Security: Bash allow rule bypass via backslash in single quotes
    P1 vulnerability where a saved Bash(...) allow rule authorizes an unprompted second command when the first ends with a backslash inside single quotes, posing a sandbox escape risk.
  6. #11695 – Tracking: Separate agent harness from execution environment
    Core architecture proposal to decouple the agent loop from tool execution processes, enabling separable, addressable runtime sandboxes. 5 comments signal strong maintainer interest as a roadmap direction.
  7. #11704 – Proposal: Official Android companion client
    Feature request for a native Android thin client connecting to qwen serve over ACP, with the contributor offering to build and maintain the MVP. 5 comments show community demand for mobile access.
  8. #11718 – Desktop AppImage Python environment leak crashing MCP servers
    Closed bug where AppImage-bundled PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH leaked to spawned stdio MCP servers, breaking external Python interpreters. Resolved this week after 4 comments.
  9. #11590 – Non-Qwen models fail on DashScope gateway due to metadata field mismatch
    Closed P1 integration bug where auto-injected metadata objects caused 400 errors for third-party models on the DashScope OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Fixed after community reporting.
  10. #11762 – /delete does not clean ~/.qwen/tmp/<hash>/logs.json
    Privacy bug where full conversation logs persist after session deletion, with no setting to disable or limit log accumulation. Raises data retention concerns for users.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11548 – feat(web-shell): connect to a selected remote daemon
    Enables standalone Web Shell to connect to explicit remote daemons via address + bearer token, with support for switching targets and reusing existing workspace/session/terminal interfaces.
  2. #11614 – feat(cli): add bwrap kernel sandbox backend for Linux
    Adds a lightweight Linux sandbox using kernel-level bwrap isolation, no container runtime/root/daemon required. Opt-in only, preserving existing macOS and container backends.
  3. #11711 – feat(core): add container execution for subagents
    Implements Docker/Podman container backends for ordinary subagent execution on Unix, with environment and agent-level configuration flags for mandatory containerization.
  4. #11206 – feat(mesh): add persistent shared-thread agent collaboration
    Introduces persistent workspace agent identities with shared thread collaboration: work assignment, interjection, result attribution, per-run history, cancellation, and review workflows.
  5. #11692 – feat(core): make web_search budget configurable and bound extractor fallback
    Makes web_search timeout configurable via tools.webSearch.timeoutMs (default raised to 120s from 60s) and bounds model input when the search budget is exhausted.
  6. #11086 – feat(serve): scope extensions to workspace runtimes
    Scopes the global extension catalog to per-workspace runtimes, with reconciled extension state, workspace-qualified daemon/SDK access, and updated extension management UIs.
  7. #11280 – fix(skills): re-apply Skill side effects on session resume
    Restores allowedTools rules and hooks from loaded Skills when resuming sessions, fixing the gap where only instructions were restored but runtime state was lost.
  8. #11538 – feat: select OpenAI wire API per model
    Adds per-model wireApi configuration (chat-completions / responses) for OpenAI-compatible providers, with support across CLI, ACP, daemon, Web Shell, and VS Code setup flows.
  9. #11242 – feat(browser-use): add Chrome Native Messaging relay
    Connects the Browser SDK to local Chrome via Native Messaging + Qwen Chrome extension, enabling debugger attachment, CDP command forwarding, and browser automation without a separate browser instance.
  10. #11722 – feat(web-shell): add PWA installability and Android development shell
    Adds PWA metadata and a production service worker to the daemon-served Web Shell, enabling installability and an Android development shell experience, aligning with the mobile companion client proposal.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data provided in this week's dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. Sandbox & execution isolation: Demand for kernel-level (bwrap) and container-based (Docker/Podman) subagent isolation, plus formal separation of the agent harness from the execution environment (#11695, #11614, #11711).
  2. Mobile & remote access: Strong interest in official Android clients and PWA support for accessing Qwen Code remotely via qwen serve (#11704, #11722, #11548).
  3. Multi-agent collaboration: Requests for persistent agent identities, shared thread workspaces, and structured background task tracking across daemon and web shell (#11206, #11636).
  4. Web search configurability: Demand for adjustable search timeouts and bounded fallback behavior to improve reliability and control costs (#11687, #11692).

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. TUI stability (React #185 crashes): Recurring "Maximum update depth exceeded" errors triggered by background agents, virtualized history, and concurrent subagent completion, causing silent crashes and lost session state (#11500, #5199, #11756, #11783).
  2. CI flakiness: Intermittent test failures, timeouts, and SIGTERM kills in shared runner environments, blocking PR merges and release pipelines without logic errors (#10490, #11777, #11736).
  3. Memory leaks & session persistence issues: High memory usage (up to 7GB) during long-running sessions, crashes with no recovery path, and incomplete cleanup of log data on session deletion (#11724, #11762).
  4. Cross-model compatibility: Silent failures when using non-Qwen models via the DashScope gateway due to unconditionally injected metadata fields (#11590).
  5. Desktop environment leaks: AppImage-bundled Python environment variables leaking to spawned MCP servers, breaking external Python tooling on Linux (#11718).

This weekly digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态周报 2026-09-14

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-09-14 00:53 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目周报 | 2026-09-14

数据来源：openclaw/openclaw | 统计周期：2026-09-07 至 2026-09-14

1. 近 7 天总览

本周 OpenClaw 保持高速开发节奏，共有 500 个 issue 更新（284 个待处理/处理中，216 个已关闭）和 500 个 PR 更新（254 个待合并，246 个已合并/关闭），体现出活跃的缺陷排查、功能交付和版本支持工作。项目发布了 3 个新版本，聚焦安全加固、更新可靠性和 LTS 维护，同时修复了网关运行时、通道投递和子代理编排领域的高严重级稳定性问题。社区反馈集中在核心可靠性痛点：进程泄漏、会话状态损坏，以及 2026.9.x 近期版本的更新失败。整体项目状态活跃，但短期面临压力，需解决 2026.9 稳定通道中阻塞发版的稳定性回归问题。

2. 版本发布

本周共发布 3 个新版本，涵盖稳定通道更新和长期支持版本维护：

v2026.9.4（最新稳定版）

  • 详情：20 次直接提交，1,558 个已合并 PR，294 位贡献者
  • 发布说明：docs.openclaw.ai/releases
  • 重点：2026.9 稳定线的累计稳定性与安全补丁，在 v2026.9.3 的更新安全改进基础上构建。

v2026.9.3

  • 亮点：
    • 更安全的更新流水线：核心与插件变更在激活前，会先在隔离的候选状态中进行演练
    • 支持符合条件的 2026.9.2 版本迁移
    • 可恢复已废弃的更新记录，无需停止运行正常且匹配的网关
  • 相关追踪：#136997、#138839、#141109、#141175

v2026.6.35（扩展稳定版 / LTS）

  • 状态：2026 年 6 月 LTS 最终版本
  • 亮点：更安全的供应商与通道边界：捆绑的供应商和通道适配器现在会限制不受信任的响应体大小，在高开销处理前拒绝超大输入，并在传输故障期间保留安全恢复能力。

3. 项目进展

本周关闭/合并的 PR 推进了核心可靠性、多通道支持、内存系统可扩展性和用户体验方面的工作：

  • 子代理 schema 修复：#146715 解决了 CLI 后端中 sessions_spawn 的 outputSchema 被忽略的问题，直接修复了 #141474 中的静默挂起缺陷。
  • MCP 子代理工具注入修复：issue #85030（6 👍）已关闭，解决了在 bundle-mcp 和白名单配置下，MCP 工具未被注入到已生成的子代理会话中的问题。
  • 通道投递修复：
    • #135111（claude-sonnet-5 上偶发的 JSON 工具调用格式错误）已关闭。
    • #145563（微信通道回复分发失败，报错 PreparedModelCatalogConfigReplacedError）已关闭。
    • #137927（内部上下文块泄漏到 Telegram 消息中）已关闭。
  • 更新与运行时可靠性：
    • #140162（Windows 网关重启时将启动缓慢的网关误判为过期进程并终止）已关闭。
    • #146958（2026.9.2 → 2026.9.3 更新因 llm-task 包所有者元数据失败）已关闭。
  • 内存与存储：
    • 功能请求 #79904（带游标的 SQLite 对话记录读取 API）、#79903（持久化会话血缘 API）和 #79905（带类型的对话记录投影）已完成关闭，推进了 SQLite 运行时重构总议题 (#79902)。
  • UI/UX：
    • #147540（macOS 端将已完成工作折叠到聊天回复上方）已关闭，提升了长对话的可读性。
    • #147506（共享插件注册测试固件）已关闭，减少了测试重复。

4. 社区热门话题

讨论最活跃的 issue 和 PR 反映了社区对核心运行时稳定性、子代理可靠性和更新失败问题的关注：

  1. #25592 - 工具调用之间的文本泄漏到消息通道（40 条评论，1 👍） 状态：待处理，P1，钻石龙虾等级，涉及安全 + 会话状态影响 社区诉求：明确内部代理处理输出与用户可见通道消息之间的边界；当前行为会在 Slack、iMessage 等通道中造成用户体验混淆和潜在信息泄漏。

  2. #97616 - OpenClaw 存在未回收的 hook/工具子进程泄漏，导致僵尸进程累积（30 条评论，1 👍） 状态：待处理，P1，银贝类等级，涉及崩溃循环 + 消息丢失影响 社区诉求：实现可靠的 hook/工具执行进程生命周期管理；长期运行的实例会因僵尸进程堆积出现运行时性能逐步下降。

  3. #44925 - 子代理完成结果静默丢失 —— 超时后无重试、无通知、无自动重启（28 条评论，2 👍） 状态：待处理，P1，钻石龙虾等级，涉及数据 + 消息丢失影响 社区诉求：打造健壮的子代理编排能力，具备故障可见性和恢复机制；用户反馈在 Telegram 论坛机器人部署中出现任务静默失败，且无任何错误提示。

  4. #91009 - Codex PreToolUse 原生 hook 中继生成 CPU 密集型 openclaw-hooks 进程（23 条评论，2 👍） 状态：待处理，P0，银贝类等级，涉及网关 RPC 停滞 + 崩溃循环影响 社区诉求：优化 Codex 集成 hook 中继的性能；用户反馈每个生成的进程 CPU 使用率达 100% 以上，导致网关不稳定。

横向生态对比

跨项目AI Agent生态对比报告

报告日期：2026-09-14 | 数据来源：5个主流开源个人AI Agent项目的每周项目摘要

1. 生态概览

开源个人AI助手与Agent生态正处于快速成熟阶段，2026.9发布周期内，各项目均在核心可靠性加固与生态扩展之间寻求平衡。在所有受访项目中，近期重大重构（会话存储、更新流水线、状态管理）引发的稳定性回退是短期首要任务，同时多租户部署支持需求、MCP（Model Context Protocol）集成成熟度，以及面向全球用户的本地化需求也在不断增长。生态正从单用户个人工具向生产级团队与企业部署转型，安全加固、运维可靠性与可扩展性受到越来越多的关注。各项目在多Agent、多用户部署模式的共享协议支持上正逐步对齐。

2. 活跃度对比
